definitions.explanation: A reddish-brown metallic element widely used for electrical wiring, coins, and alloys. Also used in compounds relating to bronze medals and copper products.

examples.japanese: この{鍋|なべ}は{銅|どう}でできている。
examples.english: This pot is made of copper.

examples.japanese: {銅|どう}は{熱|ねつ}をよく{伝|つた}える{金属|きんぞく}だ。
examples.english: Copper is a metal that conducts heat well.

examples.japanese: {奈良|なら}の{大仏|だいぶつ}は{銅|どう}で{造|つく}られている。
examples.english: The Great Buddha of Nara is made of copper.

notes:
{銅|どう} refers to both the metal copper and, in compounds, bronze (an alloy of copper and tin). Most commonly encountered in the context of {銅|どう}メダル (bronze medal).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {銅|どう}メダル: bronze medal
- {銅像|どうぞう}: bronze statue
- {銅貨|どうか}: copper coin
- {銅|どう}{板|いた}: copper plate
- {銅色|どういろ}: copper color
- {青銅|せいどう}: bronze (copper-tin alloy)

OLYMPIC MEDALS:
- {金|きん}メダル: gold medal
- {銀|ぎん}メダル: silver medal
- {銅|どう}メダル: bronze medal

CULTURE:
Copper has been important in Japanese craftsmanship for centuries. Many famous Buddhist statues, including the {奈良|なら}の{大仏|だいぶつ} (Great Buddha of Nara), are made of {銅|どう}.
